carried_forward.source: spent by earlier batches under the same authorization; see the batch abort record, which is the authoritative witness

lock_contents.note: single-writer lock for the O0 batch

lock_disposition: left in place on purpose: a crashed batch keeps its single-writer lock until the crash has been read; delete it only after recording why

contents.note: single-writer lock for the O0 batch

lock.deleted_because: the batch runner had already exited (its crash record is on disk) and the only python process alive was this annotating script; the single-writer lock exists to stop two concurrent batch writers, not to stop a finished crash from being read
lock.python_process_count_interpretation: the single python process observed at annotation time was the annotating script itself; the batch runner that created this lock had already exited, which is why the crash record was on disk to read

post_abort_annotations.outcome_note: This was not a scientific failure and no cap was exceeded. The optimizer asked the ledger for a twelfth design, which was the last one it was entitled to, then asked for a thirteenth; the ledger refused, which is the correct behaviour. The loop bound that produced the thirteenth request has since been fixed to subtract the carried-forward design attempts. Batch spend: 11 designs, 22 solver starts, 220 internal cases, 11 admitted labels, 0 failures. Authorization totals after this batch: 12 designs, 23 solver starts, 227 internal cases against spendable 12 / 24 / 240.

spend_basis.why: the ledger summary this record quotes does not use one basis: starts and internal cases are authorization-cumulative, design_attempts is batch-local

ledger.design_attempts.explanation: designs recorded by this process; the 1 design B01 spent is NOT included, so the authorization total is this plus ledger.carried_forward.design_attempts

ledger.solver_starts_actual.explanation: already includes the 1 start B01 spent; adding the abort record's start to this number double-counts it

ledger.internal_solver_cases_actual.explanation: already includes the 7 internal cases B01 spent; adding the abort record's internal cases double-counts them

independent_recomputation.rule: the latest AUTHORIZATION_CUMULATIVE record is the floor because its counters already include what it carried forward; only batch-local records it did not absorb are added, so nothing is counted twice
